rationale: Healthy-adult whole Tamr-stage Ajwa date crossover collected subjective mood diaries in 21 completers without publishing apathy or mood subscale results.

Parkinson baseline analysis with caregiver-rated apathy/indifference and caregiver burden. Unadjusted rho=.49, p=.001. Apathy drops out of the final adjusted model. No dried date exposure or intervention-related apathy change.

The two-hour change in self-rated alertness was +15.77 with the date drink versus −1.84 with placebo. Fruit maturity and comparator contents remain unclear, and alertness in healthy adults supplies no apathy-specific result.

Stress and tension declined in the single-group whole-Ajwa study; the plotted vigor score declined slightly without a printed estimate or uncertainty. Mood proxies and an uncontrolled baseline do not establish an apathy effect.

Freeze-dried unripe Khassab increased alertness and lowered calmness compared with matched yogurt. Barhi contrasts were unclear. POMS vigor was measured only before dosing. The dissertation and 2026 article report the same family.

Added Ajwa and usual treatment gave a 5.87-point mean fall in composite PANSS negative symptoms versus 3.53 in controls. Apathy item N4 is unavailable, 13 eligible participants dropped out or were excluded, and the population has treated schizophrenia.

Week-eight quality-of-life scores were 69.3 versus 66.8 (p=.015). This earlier study period differs from Syamsuddin. Baseline imbalance, quality-of-life summary scores, and the different disorder limit transfer.

The thesis abstract reports change differences for total MoCA-Ina with attention and memory differences at week eight. Participant overlap with Rismayanti remains open. Cognitive scores and GDNF are separate from the frozen symptom.

The original Parkinson study gives a separately scored caregiver-rated apathy domain. Of 23 participants with apathy, six had no depression score. It informs endpoint selection without a dietary exposure contrast.

Extracts of dried Tamr-stage fruit reduced locomotion and exploration and extended drug-induced sleep in mice. This is reduced exploratory performance under a potentially sedating exposure. The fruit preparation and apathy interpretation differ from the claim.

Ajwa pulp extract increased sucrose preference in a mild-stress mouse model, with inconsistent printed significance thresholds and separate movement changes. This reward-related assay gives no attributable Parkinson apathy response.
